Subject: Post-demo: access hardening / retention checklist for Acme Analytics

Thanks again for the demo time today, Kyle — great conversation. Quick recap and the concrete next steps we discussed on data handling and access controls so your security team has a tight checklist for procurement:

Recap (short):
- Scope: Production inference for customer PII fields (names, emails, payment tokens) plus event logs for troubleshooting.
- Residency: Primary region = us-west-2, with optional eu-west-1 for backups (you flagged compliance review).
- Retention: Session-level logs (30 days), aggregate telemetry (13 months) — you asked about customizable retention windows.
- Support access: Scoped role-based access; break-glass flow via audit ticket + OOB MFA and ephemeral session tokens.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) I attached a draft checklist (Redwood_AccessAndRetention_Checklist_v1.pdf) that maps our controls to your questions — please review and mark anything missing.
2) Contracts: you said your legal will want to see SLA terms and data residency language — I attached the SLA draft for initial review.
3) Technical evidence: Vivek will pull config examples for RBAC roles, audit log samples, and a short runbook for break-glass (who, when, retention of audit trail).
4) Timeline: If procurement proceeds, we can produce an evidence packet within 5 business days after you confirm items in the checklist.

Open items for your team to confirm:
- Do you require all PII processed to be redacted at rest? (we support field-level encryption / tokenization)
- Are any logs subject to longer retention per your retention schedule or legal hold?

If helpful, we can set a 30-minute follow-up with your security and legal teams — propose Wed 21st 10:00am PT or Thu 22nd 1:00pm PT.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate internally and loop in the right artifacts.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Kyle Morris <kyle@acme-analytics.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: access hardening / retention checklist for Acme Analytics

Thanks Dylan — good summary. A few clarifications from our side before we loop Legal:

1) Residency: We need production inference to reside in us-west-2 only initially; backups to eu-west-1 will require additional approvals and a separate DPA clause.
2) PII handling: Prefer field-level tokenization for names/emails and strict encryption-at-rest for any persisted KV caches. We need to understand how Redwood surfaces tokenized data for downstream apps.
3) Logs: Our default retention is 90 days for session-level logs unless there is an approved retention exception. Can you accommodate 90 days as a configurable option?
4) Support access: We require that support engineers never have standing IAM permissions on customer data stores. Break-glass should be recorded, require two approvers (CS manager + customer security), and generate an immutable audit record.

Next steps: please have Vivek provide an example of the RBAC role definitions (minimal privileged roles) and a sample audit log that demonstrates the break-glass event with the approver IDs. Also send any standard DPA language you have re: residency/backups to contracts@acme-analytics.com.

We’re targeting an initial pilot by August, so a 5-business-day evidence packet would be great.

- Kyle
Head of Platform Security | Acme Analytics
